messages:
katie: Quick heads-up — 30min sync starting now on Dedicated commit sizing for the EU-west fintech pilot. Main goals: pick commit (GPUs), burst strategy, and billing guardrails.
alex: on my way. can someone paste the traffic shape?
maria: latest 7d RPS tail: median 120 rps, 95th 480 rps, peak bursts ~1.1k rps (1-2m windows). avg tokens/request ~850 (chat mixed).
jonathan: flag: last month we got ~14% overage on a similar commit because fallback routed to hosted at higher price during maintenance. spreadsheet: https://redwood.link/dedicated-billing-q4 (view)
sam: important: EU-west GCP quota limits GPU allocation in single zone. if we size to 96 GPUs but they only allocate 80 in eu-west1-b we need cross-zone placement plan. that impacts latency for KV-cache.
lee: ops constraint — we should prefer fewer larger nodes vs many small nodes to reduce inter-pod networking and kernel launch overhead. also quicker preemption recovery for preemptible-backed burst.
infra-bot: scheduled-maintenance: eu-west1-b GPU capacity alert at 2026-05-14T02:00Z, expected 2h window. auto-fallback: enabled.
maria: rough throughput per A100-40G (opt run): ~6500 tokens/s sustained with quantized weights; with avg 850 tokens/request => ~7.6 requests/s per GPU for gen-heavy. for chat mix assume 11 requests/s per GPU.
alex: can you share the calc? paste snippet pls
maria: ```
# conservative sizing calc
peak_rps = 1100  # burst
avg_tokens = 850
tokens_per_gpu_s = 6500
reqs_per_gpu = tokens_per_gpu_s / avg_tokens
reqs_per_gpu ~= 7.6
committed_gpus = ceil(peak_rps / reqs_per_gpu) = ceil(1100 / 7.6) = 145 GPUs
# buffer 20% => ~174 GPUs (obvious cost risk)
```
jonathan: 145 is our hard peak — but commitments priced tiers are coarse: small=32, medium=96, large=192. 174 would round to 192 (large). cost jump is non-linear.
sam: alternative: commit 96 (medium) + burst allowance to 192 via reserved pool at higher spot price for short windows. that reduces committed monthly cost while covering bursts.
lee: recommend commit=96, burst plan up to 192 for scheduled heavy hours, and pre-warm KV-cache before window. Also set throttles to shed low-priority background requests during burst.
katie: what about billing anomaly guardrails? we need alerts if fallback > 3% of requests in a billing month or cost delta > $15k/week
jonathan: add budget alert on the billing pipeline + per-route fallback metric. I can add a Canary that simulates 5% fallback to test alerts.
ops-bot: budget-alert created: eu-west-dedicated-commit > $15k/week -> notify #finance #eng-sre.
alex: networking: cross-zone egress between eu-west1-a/b ~ $0.02/GB. with KV-cache misses on cross-zone during burst could add noticeable cost. prefer intra-zone placement and preloading cache.
maria: model variants: using smaller quantized 7B for routine requests drops tokens_per_gpu_s to ~22000 tokens/s? actually increases reqs/gpu because tokens per second higher; but quality difference for fintech may be unacceptable. propose split routing: 70% to 13B quantized, 30% to 7B for non-critical low-temp tasks.
lee: operationally we need rollout policy: canary 10% for 48h, monitor p50/p95, policy to rollback to hosted if latency > 1500ms p95 or error rate > 1%
sam: action: update capacity plan doc with commit=96 + burst cap 192 + fallback throttles + cache prewarm + network placement constraints. include pricing scenarios.
katie: agreed. jonathan pls update the spreadsheet with scenario A (commit 96 + burst 96) and B (commit 192). include estimated monthly commit cost, expected overage risk, and egress delta.
jonathan: will do. ETA EOD.
katie: thanks all. followups: 1) commit purchase approval (finance) 2) infra playbook for burst prewarm 3) alerting thresholds. meeting adjourned. :white_check_mark:
